cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says, “All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.” So Jesus sat, and He taught. I once tried to teach a room of cookie cutters how to press dough, and half of them fell asleep.

The answer is that they ask it to test Him and find a reason to accuse Him. The text says, “They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him.” So the question wasn't really a question, friends. It's like a coworker asking, “Hey, quick question,” right before the meeting where they quote your own email back at you.

The answer is True. The text says Jesus “…bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.” They asked Him the big question, and He bent down. I don't know about you, but I'd have been talking a mile a minute.

The answer is whoever among them is without sin. Jesus says, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.” He tells the one without sin to throw first. I've been pressing cookies for years and I've never landed a line like that.

The answer is leave. The text says they “…began to go away one by one…” They started heading out, and the text says it went one by one, friends. I wouldn't have walked out so smoothly. I'd have knocked over a cookie rack.
The answer is False. John 8:9 says they began to go away one by one, “…beginning with the older ones…” So the older ones were first out the door. The youngest were not the first to go.

The answer is that Jesus asks her where her accusers have gone. He says, “Woman, where are your accusers?” Then He adds, “Has no one condemned you?” The scribes and Pharisees who brought her had gone away, and He asks her about it.
The answer is nobody. Jesus asks, “Has no one condemned you?” and she answers, “No one, Lord…” Short answer, friends, and it says everything.

The answer is that He doesn't condemn her and she should sin no more. Jesus declares, “Then neither do I condemn you…” Then He tells her, “Now go and sin no more.” Two sentences, and I think there's a lot of kindness in them. I wish every pep talk came with that much care.
